target_customer: Real estate brokerages, starting with New Hampshire brokerages
problem: Brokerage staff spend hours pulling deeds, tax records and MLS data and filling out contracts by hand for each transaction.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to brokerages (pricing not disclosed)
product_category: AI agents for real estate transaction management

founders.name: Ranvir Deshmukh
education: Dartmouth College (class of 2026 per Dartmouth news)
previous_startups: CourseMe, AI course advisor at Dartmouth (acquired, buyer not named)

founders.name: Erik Peterson
education: Dartmouth College (class of 2027 per Dartmouth news)
previous_startups: CourseMe, AI course advisor at Dartmouth (acquired, buyer not named)

competitors.name: Dotloop
competitors.traction_then: Large installed base, 8.8 rating on 146 G2 style reviews cited by one comparison

competitors.name: SkySlope
competitors.what: Compliance focused transaction software for large brokerages
competitors.traction_then: Used by large brokerages and franchises per a 2026 roundup

competitors.name: ListedKit AI
competitors.what: AI contract reading for transaction coordinators

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs integrations with scattered county deed, tax and MLS sources and reliable form filling with agents. Standard engineering with hard data access parts.

defensibility.rationale: Each deal lives in a shared workspace, which gives some lock in, but similar AI agents are easy to build and incumbents already hold brokerage relationships.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were adding AI features by 2026; no acquisition of RealPact found.

market_need_then: Brokerage paperwork is manual and the industry software is described by the company as outdated. The company reports 25+ brokerages using the product on its website as of late 2026 and a pilot with several named brokerages.

branding.domain_note: Uses realpact.ai; legal entity is SignPact, Inc., which does not match the brand name.

identity.logo: Logo file on site; design not described in sources
identity.visual_style: Product-led, with each deal called a Pact
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and direct, framing real estate as having an infrastructure problem

branding.brand_signature: The Pact, the shared deal workspace that names the product concept
branding.community_and_virality: Won Dartmouth Magnuson Startup Competition in 2026-05; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name ties to the product concept, but it is generic and the legal name mismatch suggests the brand name changed from SignPact; little press on the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: RealPact is a Summer 2026 company with no exit. It won a Dartmouth startup prize in May 2026, announced a pre-seed round in June 2026, and reports 25+ brokerages as customers. The open questions are round size, retention, and whether incumbents add similar AI agents inside their existing transaction suites.
notes: Pre-seed amount not found. A Dartmouth Q&A says 500,000 USD from Y Combinator and about 700,000 USD being raised, and the 500,000 figure is likely YC's standard deal, so it is not recorded as a round. Rounds before the batch: none.
